name: Nanyang Technological University
description: Nanyang Technological University is a public research university established in 1991, with roots in Nanyang University (1955) and the Nanyang Technological Institute (1981). Based on a campus in western Singapore, it is known for engineering, science and business, and jointly runs the Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine with Imperial College London.
whyIncluded: One of Singapore's Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded Autonomous Universities and, with NUS, one of the two comprehensive local universities that most Singaporean students weigh against overseas options.

programmes.name: MSc (School of EEE self-financed coursework programme, e.g. MSc Communications Engineering)
programmes.notes: Self-financed programme; the page states students are not eligible for MOE subsidies. Minimum total tuition (30 AUs) incl. 9% GST for admission in AY2027 (from Aug 2027): S$58,403.07; AY2026: S$56,156.80. Published as one figure for all nationalities. No Citizen/PR tier (checked 2026-10-01): the page's 'MSc Programme Financial Support' section and the NTU Graduate Admissions financial-matters page it links to state the S$5,000 NTU SC/PR subsidy only 'from the academic year starting in 2024' and 'for academic year starting in 2025', not for AY2026 or AY2027 intakes, and the page no longer publishes AY2024/AY2025 totals; the NTU Graduate Admissions AY2026-27 coursework fee PDF lists only MOE-subsidised programmes. So no net SC/PR fee is stated and none can be derived without assuming the subsidy continues. Excludes miscellaneous fees (S$610 full-time for AY2025).

programmes.name: MSc in Artificial Intelligence (MSAI)
programmes.notes: Self-financed programme, not MOE-subsidised. Total tuition incl. 9% GST for AY2027/28 and after: S$65,748.80 (12 months minimum full-time), published as a single figure for all nationalities; the international tier is that figure. NTU publishes no net Singapore Citizen/PR fee (checked 2026-10-01: the programme page, its FAQ, the CCDS MSc tuition-fee schedule PDF and the NTU Graduate Admissions AY2026-27 coursework fee PDF, which lists only MOE-subsidised programmes). The citizen and pr tiers are DERIVED: S$65,748.80 total minus the S$5,000 NTU subsidy the page states for 'Singaporeans and permanent residents who enrol in self-financed master's by coursework programmes at NTU' (section 'Financial Assistance (AY2025 intake onwards)') minus the additional S$5,000 CCDS study grant the page states for 'all Singaporeans and permanent residents' 'starting from AY2026 intake' = S$55,748.80. The page does not say whether these are applied before or after GST, so they are deducted from the GST-inclusive total. Excludes the means-tested top-up (up to S$15,000 for those needing financial aid) and the 10% NTU alumni rebate. History from the official CCDS MSc tuition-fee schedule PDF linked from the page ('Past Tuition Fees'): AY2025 and AY2026 intakes S$63,220 (all nationalities, incl. 9% GST); the SC/PR history rows for those intakes are derived the same way from that PDF, which states the S$5,000 NTU subsidy 'from AY2025 onwards' for SC and PR, the S$5,000 CCDS study grant for Singaporeans 'starting from AY2025 intake' and for PRs 'starting from AY2026 intake': AY2026 SC and PR S$63,220 - 5,000 - 5,000 = S$53,220; AY2025 SC S$53,220, PR S$63,220 - 5,000 = S$58,220. AY2024 intake had separate published rates, SC S$39,785, PR S$47,415, international S$59,187 (all incl. 9% GST). Excludes miscellaneous fees.

programmes.name: Nanyang MBA (full-time)
programmes.notes: Self-financed programme, not MOE-subsidised. Programme fee for the 2026 intake on the programme page: S$89,380 incl. 9% GST (12- or 18-month programme), same for all nationalities. Citizen/PR: NBS's Fees & Funding page (ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/nanyang-mba/admissions/fees-funding) states that SC/PRs admitted to the full-time Nanyang MBA get a study grant of 10% of the tuition fee, so the SC/PR figure is 90% of the published fee. That page's fee schedule totals S$92,955.20 incl. GST without saying which intake it is for (probably 2027). Excludes the one-time miscellaneous fee of S$620.

programmes.name: M.Sc. (International Relations) (S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies, MOE-subsidised coursework)
programmes.notes: MOE-subsidised social-science master's by coursework (filed under 'arts' like other social-science master's in this dataset). Figures are the 'Tuition Fees per Academic Year' for full-time students admitted in AY2026-2027 from NTU's official 'Tuition Fees for Graduate (Coursework)' PDF (table B1.1a, S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies row, which covers the M.Sc. in Asian Studies, International Political Economy, International Relations and Strategic Studies). Citizen/PR: subsidised fees, excl. GST (GST borne by MOE). International: subsidised fee incl. 9% GST (non-subsidised fee S$34,180 incl. GST). The PDF states fees for students admitted from AY2022/23 are cohort-based and stay the same for the normal course duration. Full-time candidature is normally one year (three trimesters), so the annual fee is the programme fee; RSIS's own site (rsis.edu.sg) blocks automated access, so the duration was not re-read from it. History (same PDF, tables B1.2a and B1.3a): AY2025-2026 and AY2024-2025 full-time admits had the same rates. Excludes miscellaneous fees.

programmes.name: MSc in Analytics (School of Physical and Mathematical Sciences)
programmes.notes: Self-financed programme (listed under NTU's non-subsidised coursework programmes). One-year full-time programme taught over three trimesters, so the total programme fee is the annual fee (divided by durationYears 1). The SPMS programme page publishes one tuition fee for all nationalities per intake, incl. 9% GST: AY2027/28 S$64,841.92; AY2026/27 S$62,348.00; AY2025/26 S$59,950.00. The same figure is therefore recorded under the citizen, PR and international tiers. The page separately states that Singapore Citizens get a study grant of S$10,000 + GST (S$10,900) and PRs S$5,000 + GST (S$5,450), with up to S$10,900 more financial aid for needy SC/PRs and a 10% grant for NTU alumni; no net SC/PR fee is published, so none is recorded. Excludes the S$50 application fee and the yearly one-time miscellaneous fee.
